page: Microsoft Azure D96ds_v7 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a dedicated 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor offering 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The configuration integrates a massive 480 MB L3 cache, 384.0 GB of memory (maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio), and bundled high-speed storage via a 5,670 GB local NVMe SSD. It features no discrete GPUs but incorporates Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction sets for specialized vector and matrix arithmetic.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded performance and high I/O throughput. The instance ranks in the top tier (top 10%) for PassMark CPU score (106,546.32), multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (596.61 GB/sec), and static web serving throughput (151.5 GB/sec). Database capabilities are particularly strong, achieving 33,116.64 operations per second in PassMark database benchmarks and 156.15 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads. CPU-based machine learning inference is also notable, delivering top-tier prompt processing throughput across medium (7B) and large (70B) language models due to AMX and AVX-512 instructions. In contrast, single-core stress-ng performance and large-model text generation rates land within average ranges.

Given its dense 96-vCPU footprint, 384.0 GB RAM, and fast local NVMe capacity, the D96ds_v7 provides strong qualitative cost efficiency for large multi-threaded services that consolidate workloads onto a single instance. Tradeoffs include average single-threaded performance and the absence of GPU acceleration, which limits throughput on heavy parallel graphics or full-scale model training. The instance is optimally fitted for enterprise-grade relational databases, in-memory caches, high-throughput web serving tiers, and data transformation pipelines requiring fast local scratch storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D96ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine engineered for compute and memory-intensive enterprise tasks. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running up to 4.2 GHz, it provides 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores), 384.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 5,670 GB local NVMe SSD. The CPU includes 480 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX-512 and AMX matrix acceleration extensions, though it contains no dedicated GPUs. In benchmarks, the D96ds_v7 achieves top-tier results in PassMark CPU score, static web serving throughput, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Redis SET operations (156.15 million operations per second). While single-thread performance is average, its strong parallel execution, large local storage pool, and high memory bandwidth make it well matched for demanding relational databases, Redis caching layers, web server clusters, and batch data processing workloads.
